evidence: Cic. N.D. 2.17: magna et pulchra domus (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: The general word for size, amount and degree: big, large and great alike. Major is “bigger” and also “older”; majōrēs are ancestors (see major).

evidence: Cic. de Or. 2.131: meliōrēs fētūs … et grandiōrēs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Not the everyday word for big (that is magnus), though it can mean it: big as things grow big, vegetables, logs, children, and so full-grown; grandis nātū is “old” (Cic. Sen. 63). It also means great, powerful and, of style, lofty (Lewis & Short).
Of size and extent, often of places and buildings; Traupman’s word for “big” in the geography chapter.

phrases.latin: Māla ad crustum, nōn mollia sed dūra, nōn parva sed grandia, emenda erant
phrases.english: Apples had to be bought for the pie, not soft but firm, not small but big
make sure you have a big manure heap.

phrases.latin: aspice quam tumeat magnō jecur ānsere majus!
phrases.english: look how it swells, a liver bigger than a big goose!
